items.title: Capital Region Attracts 91% of MZ Generation Inflow - 조선일보
items.summary: Over the past four years, people in their 20s and 30s nationwide have flocked to cities with jobs in advanced industries like semiconductors and left traditional manufacturing cities. Among the 17 metropolitan cities and provinces, only three in the capital region and four in the Chungcheong region saw a net inflow of 2030 population (those in their 20s and 30s). The remaining 10 cities and provinces all experienced a decrease in young population. During this period, the net inflow of 2030 population was highest in Gyeonggi with 105,785 people, followed by Seoul with 66,561 people and Incheon with 44,976 people. Although the total population of Seoul decreased by 136,182 people during the same period, the 2030 population increased by over 66,000 people. In contrast, Ansan in Gyeonggi and Changwon in Gyeongnam, which have a high proportion of traditional manufacturing like machinery and parts, saw net outflows of 19,779 and 16,293 people, respectively, ranking first and second in net outflow among the 77 cities nationwide.

items.title: Vietnam’s biggest company, Vingroup, expands overseas as its home market slows - Greenwich Time
items.summary: # Vietnam’s biggest company, Vingroup, expands overseas as its home market slows. HANOI, Vietnam (AP) — Vietnam’s biggest conglomerate, Vingroup, is moving into global markets as business at home slows, planning nearly two dozen projects in at least 15 countries, from a “Vietnam Town” in Uzbekistan to smart cities in India and a riverfront development in Congo. But Vietnam’s once sizzling property market is cooling, while its electric vehicle company VinFast is losing money. As opportunities for large developments at home become harder to find, Vingroup, Vietnam’s largest privately owned company, is looking overseas to generate the money needed to fund its ambitions in EVs, artificial intelligence and robotics, industries central to Vietnam's goal of becoming Asia’s next tiger economy. In Uzbekistan, Vingroup signed an agreement in December to build a “Vietnam Town” in its capital, the ancient Silk Road city of Tashkent. In Central Asia’s largest metropolis, it envisions a development modeled on its signature projects in Vietnam, combining homes, shopping centers, schools, hospitals and EV charging stations.

items.title: 2026 Local Leaders: The 50 Largest U.S. New-Home Markets - Builder Magazine
items.summary: # 2026 Local Leaders: The 50 Largest U.S. New-Home Markets. ## The data highlights a challenging year for housing, with many markets experiencing year-over-year declines in new-home sales. While movement at the top of Zonda’s annual Local Leaders list is uncommon, movement lower on the list sheds light on regions that are more resilient and markets where fundamentals are working against the new-home market. In 2026, the top seven markets on Zonda’s annual ranking of new-home markets by closings remained the same year over year. Just one of the top seven markets—No. 2 Houston—grew closings on an annual basis in 2025. Of the 46 markets that appeared on both the 2025 and 2026 Local Leaders lists, 29 saw closings decline on an annual basis. In 2026, Boise jumped two spots on the Local Leaders list and was one of 17 markets to appear on both the 2025 and 2026 list to grow closings on an annual basis.

items.title: Capital Region Attracts 91% of MZ Generation Inflow - 조선일보
items.summary: Over the past four years, people in their 20s and 30s nationwide have flocked to cities with jobs in advanced industries like semiconductors and left traditional manufacturing cities. Among the 17 metropolitan cities and provinces, only three in the capital region and four in the Chungcheong region saw a net inflow of 2030 population (those in their 20s and 30s). The remaining 10 cities and provinces all experienced a decrease in young population. During this period, the net inflow of 2030 population was highest in Gyeonggi with 105,785 people, followed by Seoul with 66,561 people and Incheon with 44,976 people. Although the total population of Seoul decreased by 136,182 people during the same period, the 2030 population increased by over 66,000 people. In contrast, Ansan in Gyeonggi and Changwon in Gyeongnam, which have a high proportion of traditional manufacturing like machinery and parts, saw net outflows of 19,779 and 16,293 people, respectively, ranking first and second in net outflow among the 77 cities nationwide.

items.title: Vietnam’s biggest company, Vingroup, expands overseas as its home market slows - Greenwich Time
items.summary: # Vietnam’s biggest company, Vingroup, expands overseas as its home market slows. HANOI, Vietnam (AP) — Vietnam’s biggest conglomerate, Vingroup, is moving into global markets as business at home slows, planning nearly two dozen projects in at least 15 countries, from a “Vietnam Town” in Uzbekistan to smart cities in India and a riverfront development in Congo. But Vietnam’s once sizzling property market is cooling, while its electric vehicle company VinFast is losing money. As opportunities for large developments at home become harder to find, Vingroup, Vietnam’s largest privately owned company, is looking overseas to generate the money needed to fund its ambitions in EVs, artificial intelligence and robotics, industries central to Vietnam's goal of becoming Asia’s next tiger economy. In Uzbekistan, Vingroup signed an agreement in December to build a “Vietnam Town” in its capital, the ancient Silk Road city of Tashkent. In Central Asia’s largest metropolis, it envisions a development modeled on its signature projects in Vietnam, combining homes, shopping centers, schools, hospitals and EV charging stations.

items.title: 2026 Local Leaders: The 50 Largest U.S. New-Home Markets - Builder Magazine
items.summary: # 2026 Local Leaders: The 50 Largest U.S. New-Home Markets. ## The data highlights a challenging year for housing, with many markets experiencing year-over-year declines in new-home sales. While movement at the top of Zonda’s annual Local Leaders list is uncommon, movement lower on the list sheds light on regions that are more resilient and markets where fundamentals are working against the new-home market. In 2026, the top seven markets on Zonda’s annual ranking of new-home markets by closings remained the same year over year. Just one of the top seven markets—No. 2 Houston—grew closings on an annual basis in 2025. Of the 46 markets that appeared on both the 2025 and 2026 Local Leaders lists, 29 saw closings decline on an annual basis. In 2026, Boise jumped two spots on the Local Leaders list and was one of 17 markets to appear on both the 2025 and 2026 list to grow closings on an annual basis.
